quarto-lock

Password-lock Quarto sites on static hosting

A cryptographic lock for Quarto

quarto-lock protects a rendered Quarto website or book on static hosting by encrypting its local output at build time and decrypting it in the visitor’s browser only after the shared password is entered.

TipTry the live demo

The documentation site you are reading is intentionally public and unlocked.

The protected demonstration lives separately at:

https://lsbjordao.github.io/quarto-lock-demo/

Demo password:

quarto-lock-demo

The demo source is separate from this public extension repository so it can reproduce the intended use case: private Quarto source, public static hosting, encrypted published content.

[!WARNING] quarto-lock-demo is deliberately public and exists only for demonstration. Never reuse it for real protected content. In your own project, provide a strong private password through QUARTO_LOCK_PASSWORD or a GitHub Actions Secret.

Public extension, separate protected demo

quarto-lock
PUBLIC repository
extension + README + documentation
        |
        | quarto add lsbjordao/quarto-lock
        v
private or public Quarto project
source, data, notebooks, .qmd files
        |
        | quarto render
        | quarto-lock encrypts _site
        v
public static hosting
lock shell + *.qlock ciphertext only
        |
        | shared password
        v
content decrypted in the browser

The live example is published at https://lsbjordao.github.io/quarto-lock-demo/. Its password is intentionally published here so visitors can test the full unlock flow.

What is protected?

The lock is applied after Quarto renders the consuming project. Local HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, search indexes, JSON files, PDFs, ZIP files, and other local downloads can therefore be encrypted together.

The public protected host receives ciphertext (*.qlock) plus the small runtime required to display the lock screen and decrypt resources in the browser.

External resources such as CDNs, remote images, and remote APIs remain external and are not encrypted by quarto-lock.

Install

From the Quarto project you want to protect:

quarto add lsbjordao/quarto-lock

Then enable the extension in that project’s _quarto.yml:

filters:
  - quarto-lock

Render with a private password:

export QUARTO_LOCK_PASSWORD='replace-this-with-a-strong-passphrase'
quarto render

The password is used only during the locking step. It is not written to the generated HTML, JavaScript, or encrypted payloads.

Customize or translate the lock screen

The default interface is English, but every user-facing string can be changed without editing the extension source.

Copy the supplied configuration template into your Quarto project:

cp .env.example .env

Then edit .env:

QUARTO_LOCK_LANG=en
QUARTO_LOCK_TITLE="Protected content"
QUARTO_LOCK_MESSAGE="Enter the password to unlock this content."
QUARTO_LOCK_PASSWORD_LABEL="Password"
QUARTO_LOCK_BUTTON_LABEL="Unlock"
QUARTO_LOCK_FOOTER="Protected by Quarto Lock"
QUARTO_LOCK_ERROR_INCORRECT="Incorrect password."
QUARTO_LOCK_ERROR_SECURE_CONTEXT="This site must be opened over HTTPS (or localhost)."

For example, Portuguese can be configured with:

QUARTO_LOCK_LANG=pt-BR
QUARTO_LOCK_TITLE="Área reservada"
QUARTO_LOCK_MESSAGE="Digite a senha para abrir este conteúdo."
QUARTO_LOCK_PASSWORD_LABEL="Senha"
QUARTO_LOCK_BUTTON_LABEL="Entrar"
QUARTO_LOCK_FOOTER="Protegido por Quarto Lock"
QUARTO_LOCK_ERROR_INCORRECT="Senha incorreta."
QUARTO_LOCK_ERROR_SECURE_CONTEXT="Este site precisa ser aberto por HTTPS (ou localhost)."

quarto-lock reads .env automatically from the project root. Existing environment variables and GitHub Actions values take precedence.

Recommended separation:

.env                     → UI text / language
QUARTO_LOCK_PASSWORD     → shell or GitHub Actions Secret
WarningKeep real passwords out of Git

Commit .env.example as documentation, but ignore the working .env file. UI strings are not secret, but .env files often accumulate credentials over time.

See Customize UI in the navigation for all available strings and configuration precedence.

Test a protected project locally

Normal quarto preview is intentionally not locked. Quarto preview performs incremental renders and can recreate clear HTML in _site.

In a project using the extension:

export QUARTO_LOCK_PASSWORD='replace-this-with-a-strong-passphrase'
quarto render
python3 -m http.server 3073 -d _site

Then open http://127.0.0.1:3073/.

WarningDo not run quarto preview after locking

Running quarto preview after a locked render can recreate clear HTML in _site. To inspect the encrypted build, serve _site directly.

Publishing with GitHub

quarto-lock is especially useful with GitHub because the source repository and the published static site do not need to be the same repository.

That distinction matters for private projects.

Pattern A — publish from the same repository

Use this when the protected source repository may be public, or when your GitHub plan supports Pages from private repositories.

Store the password under:

Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret

QUARTO_LOCK_PASSWORD

A minimal workflow is:

name: Publish locked Quarto site

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      QUARTO_LOCK_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.QUARTO_LOCK_PASSWORD }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: "22"
      - uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/setup@v2
      - uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

      - name: Render and lock
        run: quarto render

      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: _site

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

The important ordering is:

Quarto source
    ↓
quarto render
    ↓
quarto-lock post-render
    ↓
encrypted _site
    ↓
GitHub Pages

Pattern B — private source → separate public Pages repository

This is particularly useful on GitHub Free when the Quarto source itself must remain private.

PRIVATE source repository
*.qmd / data / notebooks / scripts
          |
          | GitHub Actions
          | QUARTO_LOCK_PASSWORD secret
          v
      quarto render
          |
      quarto-lock
          v
     encrypted _site
          |
          v
PUBLIC Pages repository
index.html lock shell
*.qlock ciphertext
runtime files only

The public repository never needs the .qmd source, datasets, notebooks, scripts, or password. It receives only the already-rendered, already-encrypted site.

For this pattern, keep two secrets in the private source repository:

Secret Purpose
QUARTO_LOCK_PASSWORD derives the encryption key
PAGES_DEPLOY_TOKEN permits pushing encrypted output to the public destination repository

Example deployment step after quarto render:

- name: Check out public Pages repository
  uses: actions/checkout@v6
  with:
    repository: YOUR-USER/YOUR-PUBLIC-PAGES-REPO
    token: ${{ secrets.PAGES_DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
    path: pages-target

- name: Publish encrypted output only
  shell: bash
  run: |
    cd pages-target
    git checkout -B gh-pages
    find . -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -name .git -exec rm -rf {} +
    cp -a "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/_site/." .
    touch .nojekyll

    git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
    git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
    git add -A

    if ! git diff --cached --quiet; then
      git commit -m "Publish locked Quarto site"
    fi

    git push --force origin gh-pages

This is the architecture the live demo is intended to illustrate: the extension and documentation are public, while the protected site’s source can remain private.

Which setup should I use?

Situation Recommended setup
Public Quarto source Same repository + GitHub Pages
Private repo with a GitHub plan supporting private Pages Same repository + GitHub Pages
Private source on GitHub Free Private source → Actions → separate public Pages output
Highly sensitive material requiring identities, roles, or revocation Use server-side authentication instead

Why “lock”, not “login”?

This is not an account system. There are no users, password recovery, roles, MFA, or server-side sessions.

It is client-side cryptographic access control designed for static hosting:

  • anyone may download the encrypted payload;
  • a strong shared password is required to decrypt it;
  • the password is not embedded in the published files;
  • changing the password requires rendering and publishing again;
  • once a visitor unlocks the content, that visitor can still copy or save it.

For highly sensitive or regulated material, use server-side identity and authentication instead.

Security summary

quarto-lock currently uses:

  • PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256;
  • 600,000 iterations by default;
  • AES-256-GCM;
  • a random salt per build;
  • a unique random IV per protected file;
  • authenticated ciphertext;
  • Web Crypto for browser-side key derivation and decryption.

The deployment principle is simple:

Secrets enter the build; only ciphertext leaves the build.
